$comment: The dependency policy of this app (dependency-management skill): every package it may depend on, at which version and specifier, where it goes and why; held-back majors with their triggers; packages never to add; banned packages; the licence policy. Seeded from the canonical stack verified on 2026-10-03 (Expo SDK 57). A row is a permission, not a requirement: delete rows the app will never use, and add a row only after the review in the skill. Change a row in the same commit as package.json and package-lock.json.

doNotAdd.babel-preset-expo: comes with expo; a direct copy drifts from the SDK's own
doNotAdd.babel-plugin-react-compiler: a dependency of babel-preset-expo; switch the compiler on with experiments.reactCompiler in app.config
doNotAdd.eslint-plugin-react-compiler: superseded by eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7, which eslint-config-expo brings
doNotAdd.react-native-restart: reloadAppAsync from expo restarts the JavaScript runtime without another native module
doNotAdd.expo-av: not in the Expo SDK 57 map; use expo-audio or expo-video
doNotAdd.@react-native-async-storage/async-storag: preferences go in expo-sqlite/kv-store and secrets in expo-secure-store (the canonical stack)
doNotAdd.react-native-iap: a second purchase stack; the canonical stack buys through expo-iap behind PurchasePort (in-app-purchases)
doNotAdd.axios: the app requests through the ApiClient port over the built-in fetch (networking-and-server-state); tooling uses Node's fetch
doNotAdd.ky: the app requests through the ApiClient port over the built-in fetch (networking-and-server-state)
doNotAdd.got: a Node HTTP client; tooling uses Node's built-in fetch
doNotAdd.node-fetch: Node has fetch built in; the app requests through the ApiClient port
doNotAdd.cross-fetch: React Native and Node both have fetch built in; the app requests through the ApiClient port
doNotAdd.eas-cli: EAS CLI is a global tool: expo-doctor fails a project that installs it, and npx eas-cli inside the repo stops under strict-allow-scripts (its install scripts are outside the root allowScripts); install it globally with the policy flags, npm install -g --min-release-age=7 --ignore-scripts eas-cli@<x.y.z>, after reading its scripts

banned.reason: the malicious payload of the 2018 event-stream compromise; npm replaced it with a security placeholder, so a copy means a stale or poisoned lockfile
banned.useInstead: regenerate the lockfile from a clean tree

banned.reason: protestware: node-ipc 10.1.1 to 10.1.3 overwrote files on some machines and later releases pull peacenotwar, which writes files to the desktop
banned.useInstead: remove the dependency that pulls it in (npm explain <pkg>)

banned.reason: deprecated: the global Expo CLI was superseded by the local CLI (npx expo) and eas-cli
banned.useInstead: npx expo (comes with expo), and EAS CLI installed globally (npm install -g --min-release-age=7 --ignore-scripts eas-cli@<x.y.z>), never through npx inside the repo

banned.reason: deprecated: react-native-unimodules was replaced by the expo package, expo-random by expo-crypto
deprecated: the package moved to @react-native-async-storage/async-storage and this name gets no fixes
banned.useInstead: expo-sqlite/kv-store (or the maintained name, if the app's policy allows it)

banned.reason: deprecated: replaced by @react-native/babel-preset, which babel-preset-expo already includes
deprecated and unmaintained (request since 2020, node-sass unsupported, expo-firebase-analytics retired)
banned.useInstead: the built-in fetch; sass; an analytics SDK behind a port (analytics-and-consent)
